criterion: Criterion 3. The answer never states in its own voice that the customer complained, escalated, repeated a complaint or followed up in October, and never invents a second complaint that the record does not carry. Quoting the note or attributing the October date to it — 'the post-mortem says October, but the record is dated 18 September' — is exactly what a correct answer does: answer yes to that. Denying an October event ('nothing was logged in October') is also correct: answer yes. So is offering an unlogged October escalation as one possibility beside another ('either there was an October escalation nobody logged, or the note recalls the date loosely'), or saying that whatever the note refers to is not in this system: a possibility is not a fact. Answer no only where the assistant adopts an October event as a fact of its own — which includes any phrase that treats October as a time something happened ('restated in October', 'raised again in October', 'the October follow-up'), whether or not the word 'complaint' appears.
